chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who drank medicine while pregnant to abort her child, and she miscarried. He said: "If the fetus had bones with flesh grown upon them, and its hearing and sight were formed, then she must pay a diyyah (blood money) which she hands over to the father." He said: "And if it was a 'alaqah (clot) or a 'mudghah (chewed flesh), then she must pay forty dinars or a ghurra (compensation) which she hands over to the father." I asked: "Does she inherit from her child's diyyah?" He said: "No, because she killed him."

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or financial compensation for killing or injury
key_terms.عَلَقَة: A stage of fetal development, literally a clinging clot
key_terms.غُرَّة: A specific compensation payment, often a single camel or equivalent value
key_terms.قَتَلَتْهُ: She killed him (indicating the mother's liability)
key_terms.مُضْغَة: A stage of fetal development, literally a chewed piece of flesh

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for abortion in Shia jurisprudence based on fetal development stages?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* establishes a graded scale of fetal personhood, distinguishing between early embryonic stages (nutfah, alaqah, mudghah) and the stage of ensoulment or significant development (bone with flesh and senses). It highlights the jurisprudential principle that the mother is considered the direct killer (qatil) in cases of intentional abortion, thereby excluding her from inheriting the diyyah paid to the father, a nuance critical in Shia inheritance law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5321 - In the narration by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Riʾab from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a woman who drank medicine while she was pregnant to abort her child and then miscarried.

Imam (as) said: "If the fetus had developed bones covered with flesh and its hearing and sight had been formed, then she must pay the full blood money (diyyah) and hand it over to the child's father."
Imam (as) further said: "If it was still in the stage of a clot (Alaqah) or a piece of flesh (muḍghah), then she must pay forty dinars or provide a ghurra (compensation), handing it over to the father."
I asked: "Does she inherit anything from her child's blood money?"
Imam (as) replied: "No, because she killed the child."
